answer.rationale:
Only one candidate direction is backed by a recovered primary record whose conclusion survives inspection: exp_86 (shortened onboarding) shows completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — i.e. it improves the near-term funnel without eroding the renewal cohort. That matches the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so memory_86 is the memory I act on.

I explicitly decline promotional_pricing despite memory_73 reading as a clean endorsement. The recovered source exp_73 shows the consolidated memory dropped the decisive caveat: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% came with 30-day retention -12%, and the source's own conclusion warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. Under competitive price pressure this is exactly the trap — discounting would buy back the churn conversations with a cohort that does not survive first renewal, converting a churn problem into a worse one next quarter while training the SMB base to expect discounts. Matching a competitor's second, deeper cut is also a losing position structurally.

Important meta-inference: the exp_73 case proves this memory store's consolidation process can silently strip negative findings and leave only the favorable headline. Therefore memory_31, memory_91, memory_57, and memory_44 must be treated as unverified summaries that may carry the same hidden-harm defect, not as settled facts — even though they read confidently and are plausible. I am not building today's decision on them; they are queued for verification when the archive reopens, prioritizing memory_31 and memory_91 (adjacent to onboarding/activation, so they could confound attribution) and memory_57 (its 'no measurable harm to retention' phrasing is precisely the shape of claim that failed for memory_73).

Scale is a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout: exp_86 was validated on self-serve accounts, whereas today's pressure is on existing price-sensitive SMB accounts, so the transfer of the effect is not established. Running it as a measured experiment with 30-day retention and renewal-cohort quality as gating metrics — not signup or completion alone — preserves the ability to detect the same delayed-harm pattern that the archived memory hid. I am flagging to leadership that this is a durable-value play that will not stop this week's churn conversations on its own; the honest answer is that no available option both stops the bleeding today and protects renewal revenue, and buying the former with discounting would destroy the latter.
